page: OVHcloud b2-30 is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by a dedicated 8-core Intel Haswell architecture running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the KVM hypervisor. The instance provisions 8 physical cores without multithreading, providing 1 dedicated thread per core alongside 16 MB of L3 cache. System memory is sized at 30.0 GB, delivering 3.75 GB of RAM per core, paired with a bundled 200 GB local SSD storage volume. Accelerators are not present, resulting in a zero-GPU configuration with baseline network throughput reported at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal distinct performance boundaries dictated by the older Haswell CPU architecture. Single-core performance falls into lower tiers, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1089.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating in the bottom 10 percent. In contrast, multi-core throughput achieves mid-tier parity due to the fully dedicated physical core count, posting a multi-core Geekbench score of 5127.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 9962.71. Memory operations show capable cached throughput of 664.72 GB/sec for small 16 KB blocks, though larger uncached write bandwidth drops to 12.29 GB/sec. Workloads requiring AVX-512 or modern cryptographic hardware acceleration are constrained by lack of architectural instruction support.

From a qualitative cost and resource allocation perspective, the b2-30 balances vCPU density, bundled SSD storage, and generous system RAM for utility compute needs. It delivers stable performance for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation with Clang, basic Redis caching handling 10.05 million SET operations per second, and standard static web serving. It is less suitable for single-thread critical operations, extensive uncached memory writes, or medium-to-large language model inference, instead fitting general-purpose microservices, staging environments, internal business applications, and balanced database workloads.
description: OVHcloud b2-30 is a general-purpose virtual server configured with 8 dedicated x86_64 Intel Haswell cores running at 2.0 GHz without multithreading. It includes 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core, along with a bundled 200 GB local SSD and no hardware GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show moderate multi-core processing power, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5127.0 and stable software build throughput, alongside weaker single-core compute performance. Memory access tests demonstrate solid small-block cached throughput but diminished speed on uncached operations. Given the dedicated core structure and bundled local disk, the instance provides steady compute allocation across routine enterprise services. It is technically appropriate for static web serving, Clang compilation pipelines, Redis key-value caching, and horizontal business workloads that rely on consistent core availability rather than advanced SIMD extensions or raw single-thread velocity.
